clauses.text:
Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF Epwarp M. Wrrexs From Computsory RETIREMENT
FoR AGE

WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Edward M.
Weeks, letter engraver, Bureau of Engraving and Printing, Treasury Department,
who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years
by Executive Orders No. 7413 of July 10, 1936, and No. 7635 of June 16, 1937, be
further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U. S. C., title 5, sec.
715a), I hereby further exempt the said Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retire-
ment for age for a period of one year ending August 31, 1939.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 7945 of August 4, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts Edward M. Weeks from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending August 31, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The recital identifies Edward M. Weeks as a person who had been exempted for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 7413 of July 10, 1936, and No. 7635 of June 16, 1937; that earlier exemption is a separate instrument, and nothing in it affects when this one ends. The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362909, Common Crawl capture 2025-11-11T15:13:09Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7945, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on August 31, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The packet records later extension order(s) No. 8231 (August 31, 1939); each is entered as a later event, and the machine search hits for this order (OFR catalog and held-text name search) are exactly those order(s).

The order cites no condition other than its fixed period, the packet records no revocation or supersession of it (OFR catalog and U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report zero hits), and a separation of Edward M. Weeks from service before August 31, 1939 would be a fact about the person rather than an act on the order and is not shown by any held source.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no independent continuing command: it creates no report, regulation or duty, and the statute it cites is its authority, not a command of the order.","savings_check":"Savings are a fixed-period permission with no continuing consequence stated in the order or any held source; recorded as accrued during the period.","scope_check":"The order names one person and has a single operative paragraph (the first paragraph only recites the finding of public interest). One clause covers the whole order; the clause span in the dossier is the full text from the whereas paragraph through the signature block."}

Any exemption after August 31, 1939 rests on the separate later order(s) recorded as later events.
